{{Quote|After all these years, you are ''still'' a worthy opponent.''"<br />"''Your ''own'' skills remain considerable as well, Vader&hellip;particularly for a creature more ''machine'' than ''man''.|Darth Vader and the Dark Woman|<ref name="E" />}}
Shortly [[Galactic Standard Calendar|before]] the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], a '''lightsaber duel''' was fought on the [[Cophrigin V|fifth planet]] of the [[Cophrigin system/Legends|Cophrigin system]] between exiled [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[The Dark Woman|An'ya Kuro]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]]. After Kuro, known only to her pursuers as "the Dark Woman," was tracked to her hiding place on Cophrigin V by the [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hand]] [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]], [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader was dispatched by his [[Sith Master/Legends|Sith Master]], [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] to find and eliminate the rogue [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]. In doing so, Vader hoped to complete his Master's plan for the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|eradication]] of all Jedi, as [[Order 66/Legends|ordered]] and [[Showdown on Coruscant|initiated]] by Sidious himself [[19 BBY/Legends|nearly two decades prior]].

Darth Vader's arrival on Cophrigin V was [[Force sense/Legends|sensed]] by Kuro, and the Jedi Master prepared herself for an encounter with the Dark Lord. Vader found Kuro in her sanctuary and quickly attacked with expectations of cutting her down swiftly, but he was surprised by the skill with which his opponent [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|dueled]]. Kuro overcame Vader on several occasions, once through use of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to [[Plant Surge|subdue him]] with the surrounding flora and again when she [[Sun djem/Legends|knocked]] his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] from his grasp. However, the Dark Woman's own strength began to wane before the increasing [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] power of Darth Vader, and she was defeated when the Dark Lord used his lightsaber and the Force to fell a massive tree, which pinned the Dark Woman beneath it. He then moved in for the [[Death/Legends|kill]], and An'ya Kuro's body vanished into the Force. Her demise on Cophrigin V resulted in a victory for Darth Vader and one of the final Jedi deaths of [[Sith Lord/Legends|Lord]] Sidious' Great Jedi Purge.

==Background==
{{Quote|A Jedi hides on the fifth planet in the Cophrigin system on the Outer Rim. The ''name'' he whispered in my ear&hellip;was the ''Dark Woman''.|Mara Jade, Emperor's Hand|<ref name="E" />}}
[[19 BBY/Legends|Almost two decades]] had passed since the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] had been overthrown by the [[Order of the Sith Lords]] and [[Declaration of a New Order|replaced]] with the [[New Order/Legends|establishment]] of a [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]-governed [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. The [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]],<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> stewards of the Republic since its inception,<ref name="EA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> had been all but exterminated in a [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|purge]] [[Showdown on Coruscant|initiated]] by the Sith's [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]], a [[Gender/Legends|man]] known as [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]]. On the same day that the Republic fell and was reorganized into the Galactic Empire, Sidious, in his guise as [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] Palpatine, issued an [[Order 66/Legends|order]] to the [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] to execute all [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] without question, thus enacting the Great Jedi Purge.<ref name="ROTS" /> Nearly all were killed, and most of the survivors were hunted down by agents of Sidious' Empire in the years that followed. One such individual was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] female [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] named [[The Dark Woman|An'ya Kuro]], known only to Imperial [[Spy/Legends|spies]] as the "Dark Woman."<ref name="E" />

Reports of Kuro's whereabouts in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] eventually reached Sidious through one of his operatives, [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hand]] [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]]. Jade was ready and willing to dispatch the Jedi fugitive and even vied with the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor's]] [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], for the mission, but Sidious assigned the task of hunting Kuro down to Vader, given his reputation for being able to find and eliminate [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]]&mdash;wherever they hid. Vader promptly left for the [[Cophrigin V|fifth planet]] in the [[Cophrigin system/Legends|Cophrigin system]] with a contingent of Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] in search of the Dark Woman.<ref name="E" />

When Vader's [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle/Legends|''Lambda''-class]] [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] touched down on Cophrigin V, he advised his accompanying stormtroopers to maintain their position with the craft, as his mission did not require their support. The Dark Lord's arrival was [[Force sense/Legends|sensed]] through [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] by Kuro, who, in an acceptance of fate, ceased her [[Meditation/Legends|meditation]] and readied herself to face Darth Vader in battle. It was not long before Vader appeared at the threshold of a lush sanctuary and was greeted by the mysterious Dark Woman.<ref name="E" />

==The duel==
===Formidable opponents===
{{Quote|There is no ''turning'' once a dark path is taken. ''You'' of all people should understand ''that''.''"<br />"''What I understand is that some paths are ''easier'' to tread&hellip;for a ''coward''.|Darth Vader, in conversation with An'ya Kuro|<ref name="E" />}}
[[File:Star_Wars_Tales_Plant_Surge.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Kuro in combat with Darth Vader]]
An'ya Kuro engaged in a conversation with her executioner that eventually led to a philosophical debate that concerned both the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark]] and [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light sides]] of the Force. Vader's position was that the power of the dark side was greater than that of the light&mdash;something that he believed would be obvious to a being who referred to herself as the Dark Woman. Kuro, however, claimed that while the dark path was one easily undertaken, it was one only embarked upon by the faint-of-heart. Her words enraged Darth Vader, who ignited his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] and struck at Kuro. The Dark Woman parried his blow, and an intense [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|duel]] [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|ensued]].<ref name="E" />

Darth Vader had fully expected to defeat the Jedi Master with relative ease, but he was amazed to be faced with an opponent of advanced age and sufficient skill to contend with a [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]]. Kuro noted Vader's exceptional dueling talent as well before lunging at him, performing a series of acrobatic maneuvers in an attempt to overwhelm her adversary. The Dark Lord was unrelenting in his defense, and when ample distance had been placed between them, Vader reiterated his belief in the superiority of the dark side as he [[Telekinesis/Legends|hurled]] boulders at Kuro with the Force, only to have them cut to pieces by her purple blade. She then used the Force to [[Plant Surge|manipulate the surrounding plant life]] and subdue Vader with thorn-covered vines, which rendered the Dark Lord temporarily immobile. Vader was able to block the attack that followed, however, and was also able to repel the Jedi Master as he escaped the plant-restraints under her command.<ref name="E" />

===The Dark Woman's defeat===
{{Quote|I grow stronger with each passing moment&hellip;but your power has left you. Now face oblivion like all of the Jedi before you.|Darth Vader|<ref name="E" />}}
This time Vader advanced with powerful blows, but these were checked as the Dark Woman retaliated and disappeared into the cover of a nearby [[Water/Legends|waterfall]]. She emerged behind Darth Vader and caught him unawares, giving her the opportunity to [[Sun djem/Legends|knock his lightsaber]] from his grasp. Her advantage was short-lived, however, as Vader seized her arm and forced her own lightsaber from her hand. Realizing that the Dark Woman's strength was diminishing, the Sith Lord cast her aside and recalled his own weapon as he prepared to finish her. Kuro recovered her lightsaber but was backed up against an enormous tree. With nowhere to run, Vader sliced the trunk with his lightsaber and used the Force to bring it down upon the Dark Woman. Pinned beneath the tree, Kuro laid helplessly as Vader brought his blade down for the [[Death/Legends|killing]] stroke. Her body then disappeared into the Force in the manner of Jedi Masters, leaving only her [[Jedi apparel/Legends|robes]] and a victorious Darth Vader.<ref name="E" />

[[File:DarkWoman_ghost.jpg|thumb|right|140px|Kuro's Force ghost appears to Darth Vader.]]

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|Anakin&hellip;I see within you the power to release yourself from the dark side."<br />"''NO''! I seek no release! Anakin no longer exists!|Darth Vader argues with An'ya Kuro's ghost|<ref name="E" />}}
Immediately after her death, An'ya Kuro appeared to Darth Vader as a [[Force ghost/Legends|Force ghost]]. Addressing him as Anakin Skywalker, the man he was before he embraced the dark side of the Force,<ref name="SWT2">[[Star Wars Tales 2|''Star Wars Tales'' 2]]</ref> Kuro stated that in death, she proved that the light side of the Force possessed greater power<ref name="SWTV1">''[[Star Wars Tales Volume 1]]''</ref> and that she saw within him the potential to become free of the dark side's influence. Vader, however, did not seek emancipation and struck at the apparition with his lightsaber in defiance of his former identity. Kuro's ghost then vanished, and Darth Vader departed, having successfully executed yet another victim in accordance with the Great Jedi Purge.<ref name="SWT2" />

==Behind the scenes==
The duel on Cophrigin V first appeared in author [[Ron Marz]]'s two-part [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] series titled "[[Extinction]]," which was featured in [[Star Wars Tales 1|''Star Wars Tales'' 1]] and [[Star Wars Tales 2|''Star Wars Tales'' 2]]. It was later compiled into a [[Star Wars comic books|trade paperback]] version, ''[[Star Wars Tales Volume 1]]''. Plausible stories in ''Star Wars Tales'' 1&ndash;[[Star Wars Tales 20|20]] were initially considered [[Canon|S-canon]] until referenced in a non-''Tales'' source, at which point the subject matter was elevated to C-canon.<ref>{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=752#14952461|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Leland Y Chee]]|date=2006-06-04|time=3:05 AM}}</ref> An'ya Kuro's death at the hands of Darth Vader was later mentioned in both ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' and ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', thus raising the event to C-canon.

The duel resulted in one of the final deaths of Sidious' Great Jedi Purge,<ref name="E" /> an event which began officially with the Showdown on Coruscant in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']].<ref name="ROTS" /> The contest between Kuro and Vader also saw the first use of "Plant Surge", a light-side [[Force power/Legends|Force power]] that was later explained with great detail in [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s ''[[Power of the Jedi Sourcebook]]'', a guide for the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="POTJ">''[[Power of the Jedi Sourcebook]]''</ref>

At the end of the duel, the dialogue between An'ya Kuro and Darth Vader was altered between the original two-part version found in ''Star Wars Tales'' 1 and ''Star Wars Tales'' 2 and the trade paperback version in ''Star Wars Tales Volume'' 1, which combined the two. The changed dialogue is found when the Dark Woman's Force ghost appears before Vader. In the original version, the Dark Woman speaks to Darth Vader and calls him by his original name, thus eliciting a response from him;<ref name="SWT2" /> in the trade paperback version, only the Dark Woman speaks as Vader listens.<ref name="SWTV1" />
